Exercise D.S15 — Hard: Actuator limits change what can be stabilised
      
        For $\dot x=2x+u$ with $|u|\le1$, show that no admissible control can drive an initial state $x_0\gt1/2$ toward zero. For unsaturated feedback $u=-3x$, where is the requested input within the actuator limit?
        Review if needed: this section and minimisation and constraints.
        
          Show hint
          Even the most negative admissible input gives $\dot x\ge2x-1$. For the feedback, impose $|-3x|\le1$.
        
        
          Show worked solution
          For $x\gt1/2$, every admissible input satisfies $\dot x\ge2x-1\gt0$. The state cannot initially move inward or cross the boundary downward.More explicitly, comparison with $\dot z=2z-1$ gives $x(t)\ge1/2+(x_0-1/2)e^{2t}$ while the solution exists. This grows away from zero.The feedback request obeys the limit only when $3|x|\le1$, i.e. $|x|\le1/3$. The unconstrained stability calculation therefore gives a useful local design, but cannot justify global stability for the saturated plant.
